## 0.6.3 (2026-11-02)


### Release Highlights

**🚀 LoopTroop — What's New Since v0.6.2**

A reliability update: tickets keep running when OpenCode is slow, AI mistakes get repaired instead of blocking work, and the app feels more polished.

- **1. ⏳ Patience With a Slow OpenCode** — Slow permission confirmations, a cold start before the first prompt, or a busy moment before a council round no longer stop a healthy ticket.
- **2. 🔧 AI Command Mistakes Repaired** — Two common formatting mistakes in AI-written commands are now fixed automatically, and an invalid command says exactly which one it is.
- **3. 🔍 Safer Relevant-Files Scan** — The scan explores your repository with read-only file tools instead of shell commands, so it is faster and can no longer stall on approvals.
- **4. ⚠️ Accurate AI Activity Warnings** — Warnings stick to the right model, phase and attempt, and show a retry button when their evidence cannot load.
- **5. ⏱️ Clearer Timeouts & Timing** — Timeout errors name the request OpenCode did not answer and for how long, and the Debug log shows how long each permission approval took.
- **6. 💬 Themed Confirmation Dialogs** — Questions like "Discard unsaved changes?" now open in a dialog that matches the app, with clear button names and your work safe from a stray Enter.
- **7. 🎨 Tidier Interface** — The assistant button sits steadily beside **Back to bottom**, and Coverage Report tabs share one row.
- **✨ Overall:** fewer stopped tickets, clearer errors, and a smoother app.

### Summary

- AI activity warnings track current work accurately and show retry controls when their evidence cannot load.
- The Debug log now shows how long each automatic permission approval took, so slow approvals can be traced.
- Errors from an OpenCode server that answers too slowly now say which request went unanswered and for how long.
- Tickets no longer stop when OpenCode is slow to confirm a permission approval it already acted on, or when the first prompt waits for OpenCode to start up.
- The relevant-files scan now explores the repository with read-only file tools instead of shell commands.
- A council step no longer fails when OpenCode is briefly slow before the prompts go out.
- AI-written commands survive two common formatting mistakes in every planning step, and an invalid command now says exactly which one it is.
- The assistant button now sits beside the log's **Back to bottom** spot in every log view, stays put whether or not that button is showing, and hides while the chat window is open.
- Coverage Report pass tabs now share one row with Summary/Raw, and artifact dialogs no longer open with a copy tooltip showing.
- Questions like "Discard unsaved changes?" and "Delete this project?" now open in a dialog that matches the app's theme instead of the browser's plain pop-up.

### Added

- **Permission reply timing in the Debug log.** Every automatic permission reply now writes an `opencode.permission.reply.timing` line with the decision, the outcome (`confirmed`, `failed`, or `already_closed`) and the time split three ways: how long LoopTroop held the request before handling it, how long its policy and guard checks took, and how long OpenCode took to accept the reply. A failed reply is logged before the run stops, with the error. The normal log is unchanged.

### Fixed

- Keep warnings tied to the exact model session, phase, and attempt. One council member's empty response cannot flag every member, and concurrent sessions using the same model remain separate. OpenCode response summaries include session metadata and available transcript text; an empty response no longer claims a restart occurred.
- Retire timed-out coding iterations when replacement work starts, using the actual reset milestone. Provider recovery notices and failed tool parts do not end an ongoing prompt. Failed shell-command output cannot create AI timeout warnings or stop the waiting indicator. Confirmed failures and user stops end waiting; unresolved timeout diagnostics remain until success or a new dispatch.
- Restore complete activity evidence independently of the selected log tab or supplied display rows. Both log views share retryable evidence loading, keep completed evidence visible through refreshes of the same attempt, and discard it when the scope changes. Missing or failed evidence reads show a retry notice instead of silently hiding the warning surface.
- Check the evidence scope before retaining a warning snapshot, and hide the previous warning if current-attempt verification fails. Draft-view tests now answer phase-attempt lookups, and shared warning fixtures preserve retry and recovery coverage without duplicated setup.
- Keep activity pages compact with the first and last model detail for each prompt turn, plus lifecycle records. Equal-timestamp records preserve append order within each channel, and activity exports retain full selected record bodies. Indexed attribution runs once per evidence update; clock ticks update only elapsed time and deadline labels. Question waits invalidate earlier deadline snapshots, and an expired snapshot waits for a recorded outcome instead of declaring a timeout. Stable diagnostic codes and ordinary log history remain intact.
- Sort updated session status evidence by its latest update so a recovered provider no longer appears to be retrying.

- **A slow permission confirmation no longer blocks the ticket.** OpenCode acts on LoopTroop's "allow" within about 100 ms but sometimes takes several seconds to confirm it; LoopTroop gave up after 5 s and stopped a healthy run. Each reply now gets 15 s. If that runs out, LoopTroop asks OpenCode whether the request is still waiting: if it is gone, the reply landed and the run continues; if it is still waiting, the reply is sent again, up to three attempts. The check also runs after the last attempt, so a reply that landed on the third try is not reported as failed. The Debug timing line records `attempts` and how the reply was confirmed.
- **The first prompt after OpenCode starts can wait for it.** OpenCode starts a folder's instance (plugins, model catalog: 6–10 s on a cold server) while the first prompt waits. That prompt now gets the same 180 s allowance as session creation instead of 5 s, which had failed the relevant-files scan and every council vote after a restart.
- **Saving a file no longer takes the whole dev stack down.** The `npm run dev` watchdog treated the backend as dead after 60 s of silence, but a watch restart can take over two minutes on a loaded machine. Every slow restart then stopped the stack, OpenCode included, and the frontend answered "Backend not ready" until everything came back. The default grace period is now 5 minutes, and `LOOPTROOP_DEV_BACKEND_GRACE_MS` still overrides it.
- **A briefly slow OpenCode no longer fails a whole council round.** Before sending a prompt, LoopTroop opens the session's event streams, and it gave OpenCode 5 s to start each one. On a busy machine, when 8 council members open their sessions at once, OpenCode has missed that limit while otherwise healthy, so every member failed and the step blocked with "Quorum not met: 0/2". The limit is now 30 s. If OpenCode still times out or drops the connection before the prompt is sent (including while LoopTroop sets the session's model, agent and instructions just before it), LoopTroop waits 2 s and tries that prompt once more. That is safe because the model has not received anything yet. Deliberate refusals, such as another prompt still running in the session, are not repeated, and nothing is repeated once the prompt is on its way. Each retry writes an `opencode.prompt.preflight.retry` line to the Debug log.
- **A command labelled "shell" but written as a program with arguments no longer blocks the ticket.** A model wrote `mode: shell` with `program: bash` and `args`, but no `shell` and no `script`, and two attempts in a row failed validation on a PRD coverage revision. Such a command is now relabelled `mode: process`, which is what its fields describe, and the change is recorded as a repair warning. A `program` holding a whole command line, such as `npm run test`, is not relabelled and still fails validation.
- **An absolute working directory inside the ticket's worktree is accepted.** A council member wrote `cwd` as the worktree's full path 36 times, and its whole PRD draft was rejected because commands must use repository-relative paths. A path that is the worktree, or inside it, is now rewritten as `.` or the relative subpath, with a repair warning. Repeated separators and `.` segments are dropped first, and Windows drive and network-share paths compare without regard to case. A path containing `..` is not rewritten, because after a symbolic link `..` can point anywhere, and a path anywhere else still fails.
- **Invalid commands say where they are.** A failing PRD command used to report only a field name such as `shell`. It now names the story and position, for example `User story US-1-1 verification.required_commands[1]`, so the structured retry tells the model which command to fix. Bead commands report `testCommands[n]` together with the problem fields.
- Keep the assistant launcher immediately left of where the log's **Back to bottom** button appears, centered vertically with a consistent gap, in the phase log, full log, and coding views. Each view marks that spot with an invisible element that stays mounted, so the launcher does not move when the button appears or disappears with scrolling. It follows the spot when the window, log drawer, or navigator resizes. With no log on screen it keeps its last distance from the window's right and bottom edges, so it stays in its corner when the window grows or shrinks. The launcher hides while the chat window is open and returns, focused, when it closes.
- Keep the Coverage Report's pass selector on the same row as the Summary/Raw switcher instead of stacking two tab rows; when a report has more passes than fit, the selector scrolls sideways rather than running under the switcher, and keeps the selected pass in view. Artifact dialogs also open with focus on the dialog itself, so a contained copy button no longer shows its tooltip before the user hovers anything, and Shift+Tab from there moves to the dialog's last control.
- Give the phase-log and bead-log **Back to bottom** buttons an accessible name, as the full log's button already had.

### Changed

- **Themed confirmation dialogs.** Every question the app used to ask through the browser's own `confirm`/`alert` box now uses one shared dialog in the app's theme, with plainly named buttons (**Keep editing** / **Discard changes**, **Keep project** / **Delete project**). That covers closing an edited Configuration, Prompts, Projects or New/Edit Ticket window (by Escape, the backdrop, the close button, Cancel, Back to list, or the browser's Back button), switching prompts with unsaved edits, deleting a project, and the error shown when a new ticket is created but cannot start. Every way out of an edited window asks the same question in the same words. The safe answer has focus, so a stray Enter keeps your work, and focus returns to where you were once you answer. The dialog sits above every other layer, including open model lists and the shortcuts overlay. Browser Back or Forward cancels an open question, and an error message stays up until you dismiss it. A lint rule (`no-alert`) keeps native boxes from coming back.
- **The relevant-files scan is read-only.** It now uses OpenCode's file-reading, search and directory-listing tools, like the other planning steps, instead of shell commands. Its prompt already asked for those tools. With shell commands, each command needed a permission round trip to OpenCode (37 to 65 per scan), and any one of them could stall the scan.
- **Clearer OpenCode timeout errors.** "OpenCode v2 request timed out" now reads, for example, "OpenCode did not answer POST /api/session/…/prompt within 5 s". A prompt that OpenCode never confirmed now says so in plain words and includes that reason, instead of "OpenCode may have accepted the v2 prompt, but its inbox receipt could not be verified." When the relevant-files scan fails and its session cannot be stopped, the error now leads with the scan failure instead of "Could not confirm abort of relevant-files scan session".
- Both repairs live in the shared command normalizer (`shared/commandSpec.ts`). The relabel applies everywhere commands are normalized, including final-test and execution-setup plans. The working-directory repair applies to fresh model output in PRD and bead steps (drafts, refinement, coverage revision, expansion), final-test command plans and execution-setup plans, whose parsers are now given the worktree path. Stored-artifact readers and API schemas still accept only repository-relative paths.
